newsitem.title: USA: CME sets new circuit breakers with NYSE for Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: CME sets new circuit breakers with NYSE for Feb 3.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Friday it would implement revised "circuit breakers" for equity index products in coordination with the New York Stock Exchange beginning with Monday's floor session.

The new opening CME circuit breaker, or limit, is at seven S&P 500 points up or down and is effective during the first 10 minutes of the pit session. Trade will halt for two minutes if the benchmark S&P contract is locked at the limit at the end of the 10-minute period.
The old limit was five points.

The first intermediate limit becomes effective for a downmove of 15 points. That limit is in effect for 15 minutes, and if the index is still locked down 15 points after that time, a two minute trading halt would take effect. The limit would not take effect in the last 45 minutes before the close.

The second intermediate limit is triggered if the futures fall 30 points. After 15 minutes, if the index is still down 30 points, a two-minute trading halt would take effect. The limit would not be effective in the last 45 minutes before the close.

The third intermediate limit is at a 45-point downmove. It is effective until 30 minutes after the New York Stock Exchange halts trading following a 350-point decline in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. At least 50 percent of the stocks in the S&P 500 index on a capitalization basis must also be reopened for trading before the limit is lifted.

The fourth intermediate limit is at 70 points down. It is effective until one hour after the NYSE halts trading following a 550-point decline in the Dow. At least 50 percent of the stocks in the S&P 500, by capitalization, must also reopen for trading before the limit is lifted.
The fifth and final limit is at 90 points down only. It is in effect until the close of futures trading in S&P 500s.
The sole limit for GLOBEX trading of S&P 500s is 15 points up or down and is based on the settlement price during regular trading hours.
